scenario.name: LottieFiles Incident Report, Snyk & Wiz — @lottiefiles/lottie-player NPM Supply Chain Compromise, Unpinned CDN Propagation & Web3 Drainer Injection
scenario.overview: Imagine an animation studio whose lightweight flipbook player is embedded via an unpinned live delivery link on thousands of websites. An intruder steals a studio publishing pass, pushes three backdoored editions in quick succession so every site loading the live link immediately runs a hidden radio beacon, and uses that live radio to drop a fake glass login sheet directly over trusted finance pages to drain visitor wallets. In this scenario (T1195.002, LottieFiles Incident Report, Snyk & Wiz - @lottiefiles/lottie-player NPM Supply Chain Compromise, Unpinned CDN Propagation & Web3 Drainer Injection), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: compromised NPM Token Pushes, then obfuscated Bundle Execution, then dynamic DOM Overlay Injection. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Compromised NPM Token Pushes, then Obfuscated Bundle Execution, then Dynamic DOM Overlay Injection, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Compromised NPM Token Pushes `@lottiefiles/lottie-player` v2.0.5, v2.0.6 & v2.0.7
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1195.002 - Compromise Software Supply Chain)
stages.description: Using a stolen studio access token, the intruder uploads three rapid-fire compromised editions of the popular animation player onto the public shelf, banking on thousands of websites that pull the newest major version live without locking a specific version hash. Using a compromised maintainer NPM token, the attacker publishes three rapid-fire versions (2.0.5, 2.0.6, and 2.0.7) of @lottiefiles/lottie-player to NPM. Public open-source CDNs (unpkg.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net) immediately mirror the new versions as @latest or ^2.0.0 (logged in CloudTrail Event 200 with PackageName=@lottiefiles/lottie-player, MaliciousVersions=2.0.5, 2.0.6, 2.0.7, CdnVector=Unpinned @latest script tags on unpkg.com & jsDelivr so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes npm publish @lottiefiles/lottie-player@2.0.5 .. 2.0.7 -> Mirrored on https://unpkg.com/@lottiefiles/lottie-player@latest/dist/lottie-player.js (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , npm publish @lottiefiles/lottie-player@2.0.5 .. 2.0.7 -> Mirrored on https://unpkg.com/@lott so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1195.002 during "Compromised NPM Token Pushes @lottiefiles/lottie-player v2.0.5, v2.0.6 & v2.0.7" , Using a compromised maintainer NPM token, the attacker publishes three rapid-fire versions , 2 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.subtitle: Command and Control & Execution (T1059.007 - JavaScript / T1071.001 - Web Protocols)

stages.title: Stage 3: Dynamic DOM Overlay Injection & AceDrainer `eth_sendTransaction` / `Permit2` Signing
stages.subtitle: Impact & Collection (T1185 - Browser Session Hijacking / T1565)
stages.description: On cue from the live radio channel, the hijacked animation player drops a crystal-clear counterfeit prompt straight over the trusted storefront window, fooling visitors into signing a sweeping vault-transfer slip under the host site own trusted banner. Instructed by wss://castleservices.org, the injected script renders a pixel-perfect modal overlay inside the trusted web app’s DOM prompting the user to "Verify Wallet Connection", tricking them into signing an ERC-20 Permit2 approval or eth_sendTransaction call to the AceDrainer smart contract (logged in SIEM Event 1001 with DrainerFamily=AceDrainer, RpcMethodAbused=eth_signTypedData_v4 / eth_sendTransaction, DefenseControl=Subresource Integrity , SRI + CSP connect-src so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes document.body.appendChild(walletConnectOverlayModal) -> window.ethereum.request({ method: "eth_signTypedData_v4", params: [victimAddr, permit2Payload] }) (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , document.body.appendChild, walletConnectOverlayModal -> window.ethereum.request, { method: " so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1185 during "Dynamic DOM Overlay Injection & AceDrainer eth_sendTransaction / Permit2 Signing" , Instructed by wss://castleservices while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ lottie-player.js / ⇠#3 ACK 1001) from Node ③ (#3 NPM & Unpinned CDN (unpkg / jsDelivr @latest)) to Node ④ (#4 Production Web App (@lottiefiles/lottie-player@2.0.7)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 End-User Browser DOM & Web3 Wallet (AceDrainer)).

keySpecs.value: Enforce Subresource Integrity (`integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"`) on all third-party scripts so any upstream CDN mutation is immediately blocked by the browser.
